biocroxytest generates standard testthat files from roxygen comments in
your package's R source. Ordinary tests run with the package check.
Bioconductor's long-test suite can run separately.

This guide uses the [GitHub development build](https://github.com/xec-cm/biocroxytest/tree/devel).

## Configure your package

Install `testthat` for either suite and `usethis` if you use the
ordinary setup. From the package root, run the setup for the suites you use.

```{r setup-suites, eval=FALSE}
usethis::use_testthat()
biocroxytest::use_longtests()
```

`use_longtests()` sets `RunLongTests: TRUE` in `.BBSoptions`, creates
`longtests/testthat/` and keeps any existing `longtests/testthat.R`
runner in the GitHub build. If it needs to create a runner, it uses
`tests/testthat.R` when available or creates one for the package named
in `DESCRIPTION`.

Add `testthat` to `Suggests` and include the roclet in your existing
`Roxygen` field in `DESCRIPTION`. Install biocroxytest in development and
CI environments that regenerate tests.

```text
Roxygen: list(roclets = c("namespace", "rd", "biocroxytest::tests_roclet"))
```

For a long-test-only setup, use `biocroxytest::longtests_roclet` in place
of `biocroxytest::tests_roclet`.

## Generate and run tests

Add `@tests` or `@longtests` to a roxygen block. Put fast checks in
`@tests` and reserve `@longtests` for checks that need a separate run.

```{r source-with-tests, eval=FALSE}
#' Increment an integer vector
#'
#' @param x An integer vector.
#' @return An integer vector.
#' @export
#' @tests
#' expect_identical(increment(2L), 3L)
#' @longtests
#' x <- seq_len(10000L)
#' expect_identical(increment(x), x + 1L)
increment <- function(x) x + 1L
```

If you put this block in `R/increment.R`, run `roxygen2::roxygenise()`
and commit the generated files.

| Suite | Generated file | Check command |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ordinary | `tests/testthat/test-roxytest-tests-increment.R` | `R CMD check` |
| Long | `longtests/testthat/test-biocroxytest-longtests-increment.R` | `R CMD check --test-dir=longtests` |

Pass the built source tarball to either check command. Each suite loads
its own testthat helpers. Install the dependencies declared by the
consumer package, including any packages used by its test code. The
generated tests run without biocroxytest.

## Test documented examples

Use `@testexamples` with the unified roclet to assert on values from the
topic's examples. This is an alternative block for `R/increment.R`.

```{r testexamples-tag, eval=FALSE}
#' Increment an integer vector
#'
#' @param x An integer vector.
#' @return An integer vector.
#' @export
#' @examples
#' value <- increment(2L)
#' @testexamples
#' expect_identical(value, 3L)
increment <- function(x) x + 1L
```

The generated ordinary test runs direct examples before their assertions.
It omits `\dontrun{}` and executes `\dontshow{}` and `\donttest{}`.
An `@examplesIf` condition runs in sequence and skips the test if false.
Rd platform directives are resolved during generation. Inherited
examples, templates and Rd `\Sexpr{}` expressions are outside this
workflow.

## Migrate from roxytest

In a disposable copy, replace `roxytest::testthat_roclet` and any
`biocroxytest::longtests_roclet` with `biocroxytest::tests_roclet`.
Regenerate with the default `clean = FALSE`, inspect the diff, and run
both configured suites. Existing roxytest filename prefixes are retained
and generated ownership headers are updated. For shared `@rdname`
topics, tags follow their source files. Review snapshot paths and test
descriptions if a test moves.

## Check generated files in CI

Run this command from the package root after installing its development
dependencies.

```sh
Rscript --vanilla -e 'biocroxytest::check_generated_tests()'
```

The check regenerates files in a temporary copy and reports missing,
changed or obsolete generated output. Use
`biocroxytest::generated_test_inventory()` to list the generated paths,
sources and suites.

For shared assertions across suites and failure analysis, see
[Named cases, fixtures and failure replay](named-cases.html).
